analysis.title: The unintended AI winner? (AI is imploding but cybersecurity is exploding)
key_insights: Cybersecurity stocks are outperforming the broader tech selloff, with momentum accelerating, while AI-related names are being sold.

Goldman's Privorotsky flags critical PHP exploits, a major Java vulnerability and a Python supply chain compromise hitting at the same time. The note says some of this may have contributed to the prior day's AI concerns.

AI is lowering the cost of finding and exploiting vulnerabilities while the attack surface keeps expanding. The note argues this could drive a major acceleration in cybersecurity spending, with knock-on effects across software, cloud infrastructure and the broader digital economy.
CIBR has traded in a near-perfect trend channel since May, and every dip toward the 50-day moving average has been bought.
Cybersecurity has outperformed semiconductors recently, and the relative strength is more striking measured from May. The note calls it one of the clearest divergences within technology.
Catalysts: ongoing exploits could renew demand for protection, and Q4 earnings may show accelerating AI-driven security spending. The November 3 midterms could bring tougher tech regulation.
Risks: stretched valuations after CIBR's rally, broader tech liquidation, and a sell-the-news reaction if the latest threats are contained.
